subsystems.name: Active molecule
subsystems.role: shifts the epigenetic marks that change with age — for example histone deacetylase inhibitors that loosen chromatin and re-open silenced genes.

subsystems.name: Delivery system
subsystems.role: gets the molecule past the skin barrier to the fibroblasts in the dermis, where it is needed.

subsystems.name: Target cells
subsystems.role: dermal fibroblasts, which build collagen and elastin and whose behaviour drifts with age.

subsystems.name: Readout and measurement
subsystems.role: tells whether the treatment actually changed cell state, rather than just smoothing the surface.

subsystems.name: Safety control
subsystems.role: keeps partial reprogramming from going too far — full reprogramming risks uncontrolled growth.

subsystems.name: Manufacturing and quality control
subsystems.role: produces a stable, sterile, correctly dosed topical.

buildSteps.title: Map the epigenetic drift
buildSteps.detail: Compare methylation and histone acetylation patterns in young and old human skin cells to find marks that reliably change with age.

buildSteps.title: Screen candidate molecules
buildSteps.detail: Test libraries of small molecules and peptides for their ability to reverse those specific marks in cultured fibroblasts — not to reprogram cells wholesale.

buildSteps.title: Validate in skin models
buildSteps.detail: Move from cell monolayers to three-dimensional skin equivalents and donor skin explants, checking collagen production and barrier function alongside the epigenetic readout.

buildSteps.title: Formulate for penetration
buildSteps.detail: Encapsulate the active in a carrier and measure how much reaches the dermis through human skin, adjusting enhancers and vehicle until the delivered dose is reliable.

buildSteps.title: Test in animals
buildSteps.detail: Apply to mouse or pig skin over weeks, measuring epigenetic age in biopsies and watching specifically for dedifferentiation, immune reaction or abnormal growth.

buildSteps.title: Establish dose and safety margins
buildSteps.detail: Toxicology and pharmacokinetics set a dose that produces the desired mark changes with a large safety buffer.

buildSteps.title: Run human trials with biopsy endpoints
buildSteps.detail: Randomised trials that take skin biopsies before and after, measuring epigenetic clocks, collagen density and clinical appearance — the step most marketed products skip.

buildSteps.title: Scale to regulated production
buildSteps.detail: Manufacture under pharmaceutical-grade quality systems, with stability data supporting a shelf life.

prerequisites.tech: Partial epigenetic reprogramming in living tissue
prerequisites.why: reversing age-related marks with transient expression of reprogramming factors has been shown in mice, but not yet safely in human skin.
histone deacetylase inhibitors are approved medicines for some cancers, proving the chemistry works in humans.
DNA methylation clocks give a quantitative readout, so a claim can be tested instead of asserted.
getting a molecule past the stratum corneum to fibroblasts at a controlled dose is the main formulation barrier.
there is no decades-long human data on what happens when you partly reset adult cells.

pathway.milestone: lab and animal studies of partial reprogramming, and a market of 'epigenetic' creams with little human evidence
pathway.unlocks: a validated list of marks worth targeting, plus useful scepticism about marketing claims.

pathway.milestone: human trials measuring epigenetic age in skin biopsies
pathway.unlocks: evidence that separates a real effect from a moisturiser.

pathway.milestone: regulated topical with demonstrated mark reversal and long-term safety data
pathway.unlocks: a credible anti-aging dermatological product, and a test case for epigenetic medicine more broadly.

pathway.milestone: targeted, tissue-specific reprogramming extended beyond skin
pathway.unlocks: a research template for other organs — where the safety bar is far higher than for skin.
